Subject: Q: Control-plane / Data-plane split + egress provenance

Hi Priya,

Thanks for the quick intake call this week. Argent's security team has two follow-ups we need for legal & network review:

1) Precise demarcation between Redwood's control plane and our tenant data plane: which components run in Redwood-managed VPCs vs tenant-managed enclaves? We care about what can initiate egress flows.
2) Egress provenance: we need attestable evidence that egress flows originate from tenant workloads (not metadata or mgmt plane) and an ability to map external connections back to request/tenant ids.
3) Failure / rollback choreography: if an upgrade introduces an egress misconfiguration, what are the technical rollback / containment controls?

Can you provide a short narrative + diagrams and any sample logs or proof artifacts you can share under NDA? We're on a tight schedule for our procurement committee.

Best,

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Q: Control-plane / Data-plane split + egress provenance

Tom —

Thanks for the clear list. Attaching an architecture diagram and a short playbook we use to demonstrate provenance. High level answers below; attachments contain sequence diagrams and a small sample of our immutable egress ledger (redacted).

Summary (short):
- Control plane: Redwood-managed, single-tenant control plane services run in our management VPCs and have NO direct access to tenant secrets or model KV caches. Control plane can request operations (deploy, config push) but cannot originate customer data egress.
- Data plane: Tenant inference workers ("enclaves") run in customer-dedicated subnets (private VPCs for Private deployments, isolated GPU pools for Dedicated). All outbound network egress from model execution is sourced from the data-plane host namespace/IPs only.
- Egress provenance: Each inference request is stamped with a provenance token (trace_id + tenant_id + model_version). Outbound flows are logged to an immutable ledger with SHA256 digests; logs include src IP, socket tuple, trace_id, and container/pod id. We can map external endpoints back to the originating trace_id.
- Rollback: We support immediate traffic-pin to a pinned previous model/container image and automatic routing to stateless fallback replicas (CPU-based) while we remediate. Canary rollouts default to 1% traffic and can be auto-reverted on egress anomalies.

Attachments: controlplane-dataplane-demarcation-diagram.pdf (network + sequence views), egress-provenance-playbook.md, kv-cache-lineage-sample.csv

I'll loop in engineering with a request for logs sample and minimal redacted ledger rows (for NDA). If you want, we can produce a short video walkthrough for the procurement packet.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
